title: Characterizations of rectangular (para)-unitary rational functions
full_text_access: 19-page arXivv2 PDF downloaded; private research copy. Journal identity checked via Crossref/publisher-indexed metadata; typeset version not compared.
audit_scope: Targeted primary reading: introduction/conventions; Theorem2.1 and proof,pp5–6; §3 Theorem3.1/proof and cancellation remarks,pp10–11. Full19-page text, all cited Potapov theory and matrix-fraction results not audited.
correction_search: Primary arXiv history v1 2014-10-01 andv2 2015-01-04 inspected; no exhaustive correction certification.

main_results.statement: A rational p×m para-unitary function of McMillan degree d has a representation by rank-one Blaschke–Potapov factors and a constant (co)isometry, in the appropriate left/right orientation. The source allows arbitrary poles off the unit circle and hence factors from both sides; it is not solely an inner function theorem.
An arbitrary displayed product of d factors can have degree smaller than d through cancellation; reciprocal scalar factors on the same projection can cancel to identity.
In its Schur-stable/exterior-disc convention, lossless rational functions admit a minimal state realization with an isometric/coisometric colligation, unitary in the square case.

limitations: Unit-circle para-unitarity alone does not imply the all-upper-half-plane positive-phase hypothesis used in the new campaign.
Mixed-pole factors can cancel and need not have nonnegative phase derivative.
Only selected primary theorem/proof passages were read; no full-paper audit.
research_questions: Map source disc conventions explicitly before reusing a factor in the upper-half-plane model.
Use determinant degree and positive pole-side hypotheses, rather than raw arbitrary-factor count, to audit claimed state budgets.

main_results.statement: Half-plane passive inner transfer functions are discussed via Blaschke–Potapov factors and a separate singular/delay factor; finite factor phase constants can be absorbed in a unitary prefactor.
A rank-one factor is realized in passive state-space form with A=−C_out* C_out/2−iΩ, B=−C_out*D, and unitary D; successive factors are interpreted as a cascade.

limitations: Passive open-system input/output realization is not itself the closed compact-resolvent Hilbert-space proof; that proof is supplied separately in the campaign.
Delay/singular inner factors and infinite products are outside a finite rational-degree budget unless explicitly accounted for.
Full26-page mathematical/numerical audit was not completed.
